Let me analyze this OIML Certificate of Conformity.

Key details:
- Certificate number: R76/1992-GB1-12.01, Revision 3
- Issuing authority: National Measurement Office (UK)
- Person responsible: Paul Dixon – Product Certification Manager
- Applicant: CAS Corporation, #262, Geurugogae-ro, Gwangjeok-myeon, Yangju-si, Gyeonggi-do, Republic of Korea
- Manufacturer: The applicant
- Certified type: CT100 Series
- Recommendation: OIML R 76 - Edition 1992(E), accuracy class III
- Issue date: 19 September 2014
- Reference No: TS1201/0037
- Test report: pattern evaluation report P00850, 13 pages
- Pages: 4

Models: CT100 Series comprises CT100-B, CT100-P and CT100-R models. Also CT100 PLUS models (CT100 PLUS-B and CT100 PLUS-P) with modified integrated printer.

Technical data table:
- Model: CT100-B, CT100-P, CT100-R (colspan 6)
- Max (kg): 3/6, 6, 6/15, 15, 15/30, 30
- Min (g): 20, 40, 40, 100, 100, 200
- e = (g): 1/2, 2, 2/5, 5, 5/10, 10
- T ≤ (kg): -6, -6, -15, -15, -30, -30
- Emax (kg): 6, 6, 15, 15, 30, 30

This is a matrix: 6 variants based on Max capacity ranges (dual-interval instruments: Max1/Max2 notation). Actually "3 / 6" means dual interval: Max 3 kg (for e=1g) and 6 kg (for e=2g). So these are dual-interval instruments.

The variants can be identified by Max: e.g. "Max 3/6 kg", "Max 6 kg", "Max 6/15 kg", "Max 15 kg", "Max 15/30 kg", "Max 30 kg".

Model family:
- family_name: "CT100 Series"
- models: CT100-B, CT100-P, CT100-R, and CT100 PLUS variants (PLUS-B, PLUS-P). Hmm, the CT100 PLUS is an alternative with modified printer. The table says models CT100-B, CT100-P, CT100-R. The PLUS models are added later as alternatives. I could list models as CT100-B, CT100-P, CT100-R, CT100 PLUS-B, CT100 PLUS-P. But the technical table applies to CT100-B, CT100-P, CT100-R. For the model-level matrix, the columns are capacity variants, not the model names. So model_level attributes vary by capacity variant (6 variants), each applicable to all three models.

Approach: use model_family with models being the capacity variants? Or use config_level? The table's columns are 6 variants of Max/Min/e/T/Emax. The models CT100-B/P/R share the same table. So the varying axis is the "capacity variant" — I'll define models as capacity variants like "Max 3/6 kg" etc. Alternatively, use model_level with attribute rows and values per variant.

Given the schema, I'll do:

model_family:
- family_name: "CT100 Series"
- models: [
  {"model_id": "CT100-B", "label": "Base-mounted printer", ...},
  {"model_id": "CT100-P", ...},
  {"model_id": "CT100-R", "attributes": {"printer_mounting": "pole-mounted"}},
  {"model_id": "CT100 PLUS-B", ...},
  {"model_id": "CT100 PLUS-P", ...}
]

But then the capacity variants — the matrix axes. Better: keep the models as the three named models plus PLUS variants, and use matrix_tables for the technical data table, plus config_level for capacity variants? Hmm.

The rule 4 says detect matrix where attributes vary per model. Here attributes vary per capacity variant, not per named model. The schema has config_level: attribute × config-axis matrix with axis describing the dimension. So:

characteristics.config_level:
- attribute: "maximum_capacity", axis: "capacity_variant", values: [{condition: "3/6", value: {min:3, max:6}, unit_symbol: "kg"}, ...]

Hmm, but each of the 6 columns has its own set. Perhaps better to model each column as a "variant" and use model_level with model = "Max 3/6 kg" etc. Actually the example in rule 4 for R60 shows model_id "Emax=25t" — i.e., synthetic model IDs per capacity variant. So here I can do models as capacity variants: "Max=3/6kg", "Max=6kg", "Max=6/15kg", "Max=15kg", "Max=15/30kg", "Max=30kg".

But there are also named models CT100-B/P/R. Both dimensions exist. I think a good approach:

model_family:
- family_name: "CT100 Series"
- models: named models CT100-B, CT100-P, CT100-R, CT100 PLUS-B, CT100 PLUS-P with attributes describing differences (printer mounting).

matrix_tables: technical data table with columns model, max_kg, min_g, e_g, t_max_kg, emax_kg; 6 rows.

characteristics.model_level: attributes max/min/e/t/emax with values per capacity variant (using variant names as model ids). Hmm — but then "model" field would reference capacity variants which are also in matrix_tables. The R137 example does exactly this: matrix_tables AND model_level both using the model ids from the table rows.

Here the table's row identity is the capacity column, not model name. I'll create capacity variant ids like "Max 3/6 kg" and note in the models list that these variants apply to all CT100 models.

Let me define model_family.models as combining both: 
- CT100-B, CT100-P, CT100-R (base series), CT100 PLUS-B, CT100 PLUS-P.

And config_level for the capacity variants axis:

characteristics.config_level:
- {attribute: "maximum_capacity", axis: "capacity_variant", values: [
  {"condition": "Max 3/6 kg", "value": {"min": 3, "max": 6}, "unit_symbol": "kg"},
  {"condition": "Max 6 kg", "value": 6, "unit_symbol": "kg"},
  ...
]}

Wait the schema for config_level values: values[]: {condition, value}. Rule 5 says values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. The value field holds the structured value {value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers}. Hmm ambiguous. I'll use {condition, value: {value:..., unit_symbol:...}}? Let me re-read.

Rule 5: "use characteristics.config_level with axis describing the dimension. Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}." So the value objects are {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So value is the raw value (number/range/string) and unit_symbol at same level. OK.

Similarly model_level values: {model, value, footnote_markers[]} and attribute-level unit_symbol. In the R137 example: {"attribute": "qmax", "unit_symbol": "m³/h", "values": [{"model": "G1.6", "value": 2.5}, ...]}. So model_level has attribute-level unit_symbol, and values with model+value. But rule 2 says every value MUST be object with {value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers}. The example contradicts slightly — in the example, values are {model, value} plain. I'll follow the example format for model_level since it's given explicitly, but include unit_symbol at attribute level. Actually rule 2 says structured values strict... The examples in rule 4 show {"model": "Emax=25t", "value": 25} without unit object. I'll follow the examples: attribute-level unit_symbol, value as number or {min,max}.

Hmm, but "Max 3/6 kg" — the dual-interval: Max = 3 kg for lower interval (e=1g) and 6 kg for upper interval (e=2g). So maximum_capacity value could be {min: 3, max: 6} kg representing the two-interval capacities. That's reasonable: for dual-interval, Max1=3, Max2=6. I'll encode as range {min: 3, max: 6}. Similarly e: {min:1, max:2} g. T ≤ -6 kg: value {min: null, max: -6}? "T ≤ (kg): -6" means tare can subtract up to 6 kg, i.e., T ≤ -6? Actually "T ≤ -6 kg" notation means tare range extends to -6 kg (subtractive tare up to full capacity). The value is -6, meaning tare down to -6 kg. I'll encode value: -6, unit_symbol: "kg" with attribute "maximum_subtractive_tare" or "tare_limit". Given the minus sign in the table: "- 6". I'll set value -6.

Emax: 6, 6, 15, 15, 30, 30 kg. Note: Emax refers to actual measuring range and does not include dead load — that's a note, could be a footnote? It's a "Note:" not numbered footnote. I could add footnotes entry with marker "note" or just keep in description. Maybe add to footnotes as marker "1)"? No — don't fabricate markers. I'll capture in matrix_tables description.

Components: load cell CAS model TP. Record as component: role "load cell", type_designations ["TP"], characteristics: capacities as per table — the capacities match the Emax values? "capacities as per following table" — the table includes Emax (kg) row, so load cell capacities correspond. I'll note characteristics {capacity_per_table: ...} maybe keep simple: characteristics: {"capacity": {"reference": "per technical data table"}}. Hmm, better to just list type_designations and maybe model "TP". Keep it simple.

Devices: list of devices — could go into certified_type.description. I'll include construction and devices in description text.

Characteristics type_level:
- accuracy_class: "III" (string)
- power_supply_voltage: 230 V (AC)
- power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz
- power_supply_type: "AC" (mains) — also battery 12V. Add secondary_power_supply: {"type": "internal rechargeable battery", "value": 12, unit "V"}? I'll add "battery_voltage": 12 V and battery_type: "internal rechargeable".
- temperature_range: {min:-10, max:40} °C
- initial_zero_setting_device: ≤20% of Max → value {min:null,max:20}, unit "%"
- semi_automatic_zero_setting_device: ≤4% of Max → {max:4} "%"
- zero_tracking_device: ≤4% of Max → {max:4} "%"
- software_version: "1.xx"
- price_computing: true? These are devices. Maybe keep description.

Interfaces: list — could be in description or as components? Keep in description.

Test reports: id "P00850", pages 13, role "type_evaluation_report" (pattern evaluation report). Rule: id canonical. P00850.

Recommendation: id "R76", edition 1992, scheme "A"? Scheme A or B — MAA certificates. This is an OIML MAA certificate (Logo: OIML — MUTUAL ACCEPTANCE ARRANGEMENT). MAA certificates are scheme B? Actually under the OIML Certification System (OIML-CS), Scheme A is basic, Scheme B is MAA. The MAA logo indicates... Hmm. The certificate is issued under MAA — "OIML R76 MAA Rev. 1 01 April 2011" appears at bottom of page 1. So scheme: "B". I'll set scheme "B".

accuracy_classes: ["III"].

Revision history: from Certificate History table:
- revision "0"? First issued: R76/1992-GB1-12.01, 12 January 2012, "Certificate first issued" → revision "0"
- rev 1, 12 March 2012, Preset Tare device allowed
- rev 2, 06 August 2012, Alternative manufacturers added

Page total: 4. Member State: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. date_issued: 19 September 2014 → "2014-09-19". oiml_issuer_id: not given. The "0135" near UKAS logo? That's probably a UKAS number, not issuer ID. Skip.

Reference No: TS1201/0037 — this is NMO's project/reference number → project_number? Schema has project_number at certificate level. I'll use "TS1201/0037".

Issuing authority address: Stanton Avenue, Teddington, TW11 0JZ, United Kingdom. Phone: +44 (0)20 8943 7272. Website: www.gov.uk/nmo. Person responsible: Paul Dixon, title Product Certification Manager. Signatory P R Dixon for Chief Executive.

Alternative manufacturers — these are manufacturers of the certified type too. Schema has manufacturers[] — I'll include CAS Corporation (the applicant, "Manufacturer: The applicant") plus the three alternative manufacturers:

model_level entries:

Hmm — dual interval: e values are pairs (e1/e2). For single-interval variants, single value.

Since these are dual-interval instruments, Max = Max1/Max2 and e = e1/e2. Range representation is fine.
